scope: remote anonymous publication and source-candidate disclosure review; read-only HTTP and retained browser evidence

G6.11.claim: The selected published load and stability results are bounded single-validator experiments, not Solana-wide throughput or decentralisation benchmarks.
G6.11.basis: The publicly accessible source-candidate load report explicitly limits its 20 SDK sessions and 200 operations to one validator and disclaims chain-wide capacity. The terminal report describes one source-built test validator with a bounded valueless browser workload and excludes mainnet approval. The published README identifies the single project-operated validator and separates the completed stability run from remaining release requirements.
G6.11.scopeLimit: Review of the selected published workload disclosures and README, not an audit of every external communication or a new performance measurement.

G7.03.claim: The public frontend URLs, actual genesis, software manifest, single operator count and experimental limitations are anonymously accessible.
G7.03.basis: Both network-page URLs returned HTTP 200 without credentials. The canonical network endpoint returned the frozen genesis, remote experimental mode, operatorCount 1 and hasMonetaryValue false. The public dependency manifest exactly matches the candidate hash; the current runtime endpoint matches the complete frozen identity including the source-built engine manifest. Published README bytes identify one validator and valueless test assets. Retained final-browser evidence separately establishes the earlier rendered production journeys.
G7.03.scopeLimit: Current checks establish HTTP access, published bytes and identity fields. They do not re-render the application, verify every link or certify accessibility; prior rendered-browser results retain their own observation times.

limitations: These HTTP observations are point-in-time access and byte checks, not continuous monitoring or a new rendered browser regression.
The dependency manifest is the frozen application dependency record; the runtime endpoint separately binds the current source-built engine binaries.
No old-candidate acceptance is carried over. Deadline compliance, machine specification publication and other unreviewed requirements are not inferred.
